ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image has two schematic diagrams of square rooms, with the room side length labeled S. In Figure 1, the table is located in the upper-left corner of the room, and the tabletop is a rectangle, with the horizontal side labeled 10 ft and the vertical side labeled 8 ft. In Figure 2, the table is still in the upper-left corner, but has been rotated into a position with horizontal side 8 ft and vertical side 10 ft. Reasoning: Regard the table as a rigid 10 ft by 8 ft rectangle. During the movement it is not tilted and not taken apart, so it can be continuously rotated in the plane; let the angle between the 10 ft long side and the horizontal line be θ, with θ continuously changing from 0° to 90°. At angle θ, the table's horizontal projection width is 10 cos θ + 8 sin θ, and the vertical projection height is 10 sin θ + 8 cos θ. To be able to fit into an S by S square room, throughout the whole process these two projections must both not exceed S. For 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°, the maximum value of the function 10 cos θ + 8 sin θ is sqrt(10^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(164), and the maximum value of the function 10 sin θ + 8 cos θ is likewise sqrt(164). Therefore S ≥ sqrt(164) ≈ 12.81 is needed. S must be taken as an integer, so the smallest integer is 13.

Model the table during the move as an 8 by 10 rigid rectangle whose long side makes an angle θ with the horizontal, where θ must vary continuously from 0° to 90°. At angle θ, its axis-aligned horizontal and vertical spans are 10 cos θ + 8 sin θ and 10 sin θ + 8 cos θ. For the table to fit in an S by S square at every stage, both spans must be at most S for every θ. Maximize these span functions on 0 ≤ θ ≤ 90°; each has maximum sqrt(10^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(164) ≈ 12.81. Therefore S must be at least sqrt(164), and the smallest integer S is 13.

method.method_draft: Read the figures as showing the same 8' by 10' table in one corner before and after being rotated 90 degrees in the plane of the floor. Use a diagonal obstruction. The table has diagonal length d = sqrt(8^2 + 10^2) = sqrt(164). During any continuous in-plane rotation from Figure 1 to Figure 2, one diagonal of the table changes direction by 90 degrees, so by continuity it must at some instant be exactly horizontal or exactly vertical. At that instant, the square room must contain a horizontal or vertical segment of length d, so S ≥ d. Conversely, if S ≥ d, place the table’s center at the room’s center and rotate it there: all four vertices stay within the circumcircle of radius d/2, which lies inside an S by S square when S ≥ d. Since the initial and final corner positions can be reached by sliding the rectangle before and after the rotation when S > 10, this gives the threshold S = sqrt(164). Hence the least integer S is 13.
